hyperedges.label: Primitives forming the shared rule spine

nodes.label: content-critic reviewer
nodes.rationale: Read-only reviewer of rule, voice, fairness, pedagogy, data shape and evidence conformance; it never invents course facts from memory.

nodes.label: Content rule catalogue (N/P/C/H/D/V)
nodes.rationale: Rules are immutable without the user's agreement and every reviewer finding or editor brief cites their IDs.

nodes.label: Counters and stuckness keys
nodes.rationale: counters is free-form at load; only conditions interpret hints-shown, failed-attempts and turns-since. Counters are never pruned so the save keeps a complete audit trail.

nodes.label: Hazard types (entry trap, timed hazard, action trap)
nodes.norm_label: hazard types (entry trap, timed hazard, action trap)
nodes.rationale: A definition's schedule is not active until an effect registers it: room entry applies a schedule effect adding the ScheduledEvent to GameStateDto.schedule, after which Scheduler owns the countdown.

nodes.label: Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Modelled on the TADS fuse and daemon: Scheduler.tick runs first in phase 4, and all scheduled state is serialised in GameStateDto.schedule so a reload resumes timers accurately.

nodes.label: hint-penalty-applied
nodes.rationale: The default scorePenalty is 0 because penalties discourage the behaviour a revision tool should encourage. If content opts in, HintSystem emits the event and ScoreTracker (the sole score writer) applies it.

nodes.label: ScoreTracker
nodes.rationale: ScoreTracker remains the only writer of score and progress: it awards from achievement events (room-entered, puzzle-solved, quiz-ended, hint-penalty-applied) rather than writing a number.

nodes.label: Per-puzzle scoring
nodes.rationale: Several puzzles may map to one topic and each awards its own points within the topic's maxScore budget; only covered topics with evidence are scoreable, and score is written by ScoreTracker, not PuzzleSystem.

nodes.label: Architecture decision log
nodes.rationale: Records settled choices such as versioned JSON saves with SCHEMA_VERSION 1, no migration before public release, build order, and the win condition.

nodes.label: Architecture design principles
nodes.rationale: Static-first, OOP with strict TS, separation of concerns, data-driven content, one source of truth, explicit persistence and testability. The core is DOM-free and deterministic so it can be unit-tested without a browser.

nodes.label: Random port
nodes.rationale: Quiz order and varied NPC replies need randomness, but core must stay deterministic for saves and tests: a seeded PRNG seed lives in GameStateDto.rngSeed, advances on each draw and is saved. No Math.random() anywhere in src/core.

nodes.label: PuzzlePhase / three-phase state
nodes.rationale: Multi-step tasks are represented by one puzzle per step in the dependency graph; a puzzle may be activated before it is solved. EffectApplier sets the phase to solved before emitting puzzle-solved, which prevents double-firing.

nodes.label: Hazard failure consequences
nodes.rationale: Failure effects may lose a life (change-lives -1), return to the level start (move-player) or reset level-local flags via set-flag. Failed hazards do not reset puzzle state, and hints are not offered for hazards because they are brief penalties, not puzzles.

nodes.label: answer command (1-based)
nodes.rationale: answer N is 1-based in the UI; the parser stores option = N - 1. There is no time limit because the game is turn-based and no clock exists in core; answer outside a quiz gives a friendly message, never a parser error.

nodes.label: quizAttempts / QuizStateDto
nodes.rationale: Retry limits are stored in quizAttempts: Record<quizId, number> rather than a single QuizStateDto.attempts field; the count increments at quiz start and persists across attempts.

nodes.label: HintSequence
nodes.rationale: Targets may include GCSE spec topic IDs so the ScorePanel can label the revision area a hint belongs to; HintCatalogue resolves by ID and by target.

nodes.label: HintSystem
nodes.rationale: Hints never write puzzle/quiz state and never solve a puzzle; they only emit hint-shown events and may adjust counters.

nodes.label: Actor
nodes.rationale: Actor is a class with identity and behaviour (unlike data-only ActorState), consistent with architecture.md §5; its serialised shape is NpcStateDto.

nodes.label: ActorState
nodes.rationale: Data, not behaviour: stateDesc appends to examine text and specialDesc appears in the room listing; onEnter and onExit hold Effects.

nodes.label: ConversationNode (ConvNode)
nodes.rationale: ConvNodes are included in v1 because the game is a revision tool: a forced question is exactly how a student is made to engage with a concept. A defaultTopicId keeps the player in the node until a special topic matches.

nodes.label: Condition
nodes.rationale: Conditions are pure data; missing flags and IDs evaluate to false, never throw (noUncheckedIndexedAccess). The same evaluator powers pre-turn validation and post-turn reaction checks.

nodes.label: Counter key namespace
nodes.rationale: counter-at-least is deliberately generic: hints-shown:<hintId> is incremented by show-hint, failed-attempts:<quizId> by a wrong quiz answer, and turns-since:<puzzleId> each turn after a puzzle first becomes active. Counters are never pruned — a complete audit trail is kept.

nodes.label: transfer-item effect
nodes.rationale: Uses the reserved owner ID 'player'; other owners are actor or room IDs. It updates both inventories atomically, so no separate remove/grant pair is needed for give/show, and every item has exactly one owner.

nodes.label: Trigger
nodes.rationale: A definition may have one trigger; multiple conditions combine with 'all'. Triggers are checked in phase 4 against buffered events and final state.

nodes.label: Quiz combat (adversarial quiz)
nodes.rationale: There is no stat-based combat: 'combat' is an adversarial quiz where an NPC questions the player on GCSE material. It is both a damage source and the main revision loop, and reuses the conversation plumbing from a ConversationNode special topic via the start-quiz effect.

nodes.label: Quiz pass scoring
nodes.rationale: A quiz pass awards its own declared score once, guarded by the quiz-passed:<quizId> flag that backs the quiz-passed condition; topic-completed itself awards no points. A failed quiz resets position and lives only, never topic progress.

nodes.label: Conversation flow (implicit start, no timeout)
nodes.rationale: talk-to or any conversational verb implicitly starts a conversation; bye or leaving the room ends it. There is deliberately no turn timeout — no implicit 'you drifted away' farewell — and topic matching happens in phase 3.

nodes.label: Puzzle Dependency Graph
nodes.rationale: Ron Gilbert / Noah Falstein's Puzzle Dependency Graph is an authoring and testing tool, not runtime machinery: a DAG where a cycle means a softlock, dependsOn is the edge list, a Vitest suite checks acyclicity/reachability/unique IDs/valid topic IDs, and narrative text may only reference a puzzle's ancestor graph.

nodes.label: Adaptive hints (escalating levels)
nodes.rationale: Follows TADS's adaptive hint idea: hints escalate in levels and can be unlocked by evidence the player is stuck. Independent unlock conditions must not skip levels. There is no 'reveal the answer' level — the player must still supply an answer to pass a quiz.

nodes.label: Hint cooldown and context resolution
nodes.rationale: Context resolves by explicit targetId, then active quiz, then current room; there is no separate active-puzzle context field. Repeated requests are rate-limited by cooldownTurns using lastShownTurn.

nodes.label: learn-topic / knowsAbout gating
nodes.rationale: Adapted from TADS 3's knowsAbout: the player cannot ask about the ring until the NPC mentions it. Where the player could discover a thing independently, a second topic with a negated npc-knows/has-item condition is defined (the TADS AltTopic pattern).

nodes.label: TopicResolver
nodes.rationale: NameResolver resolves object IDs but cannot resolve free-text topics, so TopicResolver sits beside it and takes the raw noun phrase; unknown topics never crash or say 'parser error'.

nodes.label: Action-set flags authoring rule
nodes.rationale: Requirements must be action-set flags, not mere possession: 'has the brass key' must not auto-solve 'unlock the door'. The use key on door handler sets door-unlocked and that flag is the requirement. Possession is only valid when the solution genuinely is carrying something to a place.

nodes.label: ContentBundle and catalogues
nodes.rationale: All definitions are declarative data under src/content/, never hard-coded in engine classes. Catalogues expose getById(id), all and targeted lookups, bundled into an injected ContentBundle so tests can inject fixtures. Content validation enforces globally unique object and NPC aliases so NameResolver never has to guess.

nodes.label: Catalogue<T> (declaration-order registry)
nodes.rationale: The `all` array exists because shared-rules.md §11 requires declaration-order evaluation; getById returns undefined rather than throwing for missing IDs.

nodes.label: Canonical Command union
nodes.rationale: This is the single canonical union replacing the partial lists in architecture.md, npcs.md, combat.md and hints.md; meta actions are deliberately excluded so they never enter core dispatch or advance the turn.

nodes.label: ContentBundle
nodes.rationale: One injected ContentBundle of typed catalogues keeps the engine content-agnostic; all definitions are declarative data under src/content and are validated at boot so the game never boots with broken IDs or aliases.

nodes.label: Game façade
nodes.rationale: Game owns the whole turn pipeline and intercepts meta actions so behaviour is identical from a button or the terminal; it never throws on bad input and turns unparseable text into an 'unknown' command with a friendly message.

nodes.label: MetaAction union
nodes.rationale: Typed save/load/download/import/restart are aliases for SaveControls buttons, intercepted by Game before core dispatch; they never advance the turn.

nodes.label: Per-puzzle scoring
nodes.rationale: Each solved puzzle, quiz pass and first room visit awards its own declared points within SpecTopic.maxScore; topic-completed awards nothing. Idempotency is derived from existing state so no new persisted field is needed.

nodes.label: Stub content fixture
nodes.rationale: A one-area, two-room stub exists only so the app boots and Playwright has a deterministic world; it is data, not engine code, and is deleted when the first real area is converted.

nodes.label: Title screen overlay
nodes.rationale: v1 has a title screen as a UI overlay, not a persisted state; it is removed only after the first event batch is published so the player never sees an empty terminal, and Continue is disabled without a valid save.

nodes.label: validateContent
nodes.rationale: Vitest runs the same function against small fixtures and the real catalogues so boot validation and test validation cannot drift.

nodes.label: GameViewData
nodes.rationale: ScorePanel needs current aggregate state and is forbidden from computing scores itself, so Game.getViewData() is the state channel while events drive the transcript and transient panels.

nodes.label: Bootstrap (src/main.ts)
nodes.rationale: The composition root constructs and wires everything; it must not assume the site is served from the domain root because Vite sets base: '/CompSciQuest/'.

nodes.label: One-command turn pipeline
nodes.rationale: Resolve → Validate → Execute → React → Observe → Publish; per-turn event buffering gives deterministic ordering and prevents the UI seeing half-updated state.

nodes.label: ID and alias registry
nodes.rationale: The bible owns one registry of kebab-case kind-prefixed IDs; aliases are unique across all objects and NPCs so no disambiguation prompt is needed.

nodes.label: Structural validation gates
nodes.rationale: content-ids, quiz-content, puzzle-graph, hint-content, hazard-content, npc-content and score-content gates must pass before a card set is accepted; specification only in this draft.

nodes.label: LoadResult and LoadFailureReason
nodes.rationale: A typed union with five reasons lets SaveControls map each failure to a distinct friendly message; a bad import never partially overwrites the live save.

nodes.label: Save quarantine
nodes.rationale: On boot only a corrupt live save is quarantined rather than discarded, in a single slot that is never overwritten, so the player can still start fresh and download the raw text for recovery.

nodes.label: Save validation contract
nodes.rationale: Required keys and types are checked, unknown extra keys are ignored for additive v1 compatibility, and validation runs JSON parse → version → shape → content references.

nodes.label: Rule spine (shared rule spine)
nodes.rationale: NPCs, hazards, quiz combat, puzzles and hints all reduce to the same primitive — when a condition holds, apply a set of effects, possibly on a schedule. Building five separate engines would duplicate the same machinery five times, so one small rule spine in src/core/ is defined and thin domain systems sit on top of it.

nodes.label: Schema v1 without migration
nodes.rationale: There is no schema migration step yet: SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 and SaveManager does not migrate. Old v1 saves made before the new fields existed fail strict validation, which is accepted while the game is unreleased; versioning is revisited before public release.

nodes.label: Effect-to-event mapping
nodes.rationale: Every effect produces at least one buffered event; an effect that needs to speak includes its own message effect alongside the state-changing one.

nodes.label: EventBus
nodes.rationale: Publishes a whole turn's buffered batch so the UI never sees half-updated state; unchanged from architecture.md §7.

nodes.label: Canonical GameEvent union
nodes.rationale: Consolidates the seven baseline variants, thirteen subsystem variants and the §9 bookkeeping events into one union so every state change is explainable in the output log.

nodes.label: ScoreTracker
nodes.rationale: Sole writer of AreaProgress.earnedScore; score-changed.total is the sum of area totals at the moment of observation and is never read from a save.

nodes.label: Session win/lose check
nodes.rationale: Runs in phase 5 after ScoreTracker.observe so end events carry the final score; a reloaded end state does not re-emit game-won or game-over.

nodes.label: SpecTopicCatalogue
nodes.rationale: getByAreaId is what restore and the ScorePanel need to refresh AreaProgress.maxScore from the live content.

nodes.label: Layer dependency rule
nodes.rationale: Imports point downward: core imports nothing from application, UI, storage or the DOM; the only outward import is a type-only StorageAdapter port, and EventBus is the only upward channel.

nodes.label: Layered architecture
nodes.rationale: Adapters (UI, storage) sit outside application services, which depend on a pure core engine, which in turn consumes declarative content definitions.

nodes.label: SpecTopic
nodes.rationale: Mirrors docs/coverage/COVERAGE.md: status and evidence decide scoreability and the win check; roomIds let a topic span several rooms.

nodes.label: Restore-time derivation
nodes.rationale: Score is derived from area totals and AreaProgress.maxScore is refreshed from the live SpecTopicCatalogue at restore, so older saves adjust when content changes; restore derives but never emits events.

nodes.label: GameState
nodes.rationale: Runtime counterpart of the canonical DTO with createInitial/fromDto/toDto factories; score is derived at restore rather than stored, while status is persisted.

nodes.label: SaveManager
nodes.rationale: Assembles the SaveDto envelope with version and savedAt, validates and restores, and catches parse errors; no migration is implemented yet.

nodes.label: Static-first site
nodes.rationale: No backend calls: localStorage is the live store and JSON files are the portable store because the game is a fully static GitHub Pages site.

nodes.label: Item ownership invariant
nodes.rationale: Each item ID occurs in exactly one owner list — player, NPC or room state — so there is no central owner map; transfer-item updates both lists atomically.

nodes.label: Persisted shape (GameStateDto)
nodes.rationale: DTOs may contain only plain strings, numbers, booleans, arrays and records; optional fields are omitted rather than set to undefined, and score is not stored.

nodes.label: SaveDto envelope
nodes.rationale: version (literal 1) plus savedAt from the injected Clock wrap GameStateDto; imports preserve the original savedAt and dated filenames prevent exports overwriting each other.

nodes.label: StorageAdapter port
nodes.rationale: An interface-only seam injected with the catalogues and Clock into SaveManager so it is testable with in-memory fakes and a fake clock.

nodes.label: HazardCatalogue
nodes.rationale: Exposes getById(id) and getForRoom(roomId) so HazardSystem does not scan the whole content set every turn; the level-start room is explicitly declared per world/area as startRoomId on AreaDefinition, not derived from the world graph.

nodes.label: HazardSystem
nodes.rationale: Runs in phase 4 of the turn pipeline after the scheduler and before NPC reactions: iterate definitions in declaration order, skip once/cooldown cases, evaluate trigger then when, and apply effects through EffectApplier. Hazards never write score or call Session directly.

nodes.label: PuzzleSystem
nodes.rationale: Runs in phase 4 of the turn pipeline after hazards and NPC reactions, before auto-hints. Puzzle progress is owned solely by PuzzleSystem — a hazard teleport or flag reset never reverts it.

nodes.label: EffectApplier
nodes.rationale: EffectApplier.apply is the only mutator of the effect-controlled fields and emits at least one buffered event per effect, so every state change is explainable in the output log. Handlers and domain systems return effects rather than writing state directly.

nodes.label: Silent cascade skip
nodes.rationale: A reaction effect can enable another rule, but each rule ID may fire at most once per turn and one extra reaction pass is allowed (a third is not). The skip is silent to the player and asserted only in tests.

nodes.label: Turn pipeline (buffered events)
nodes.rationale: Events are buffered for the whole turn and published once, after all state is final. This is the TADS 'transcript' idea: deterministic output, no UI rendering of half-updated state, and explicit observer order. Phase 4 is ordered: scheduled events, hazards, NPC reactions, puzzle completion, auto-hints. ScoreTracker runs before Session so game-over and game-won carry the final score.

nodes.label: Content authority order
nodes.rationale: Course facts come from the exam spec via COVERAGE.md before the bible; subsystem docs own data shape, while this file owns authoring practice and the bible owns creative choices.

nodes.label: Content bible
nodes.rationale: docs/content/content-bible.md is co-authored with the user and changed only with their approval; it owns the premise, pillars, cast, topic allocation, PDG and ID/alias registry.

nodes.label: Design card
nodes.rationale: A Markdown file under docs/content/<area>/ specifying one kind of content; writers produce cards only and never edit engine code or configs.

nodes.label: pck-reviewer reviewer
nodes.rationale: Independent read-only subject-matter check against wjec-unit1.md and COVERAGE.md; does not use the web, does not review voice or data shape, and does not design the fix.

nodes.label: Content workflow gates W1-W6
nodes.rationale: No writer is launched before bible approval; independent briefs run in parallel, two independent reviewers must pass, and integration updates COVERAGE.md and status.md.
